newsitem.title: USA: Buffton says EPA asks $1.2 mln for clean-up.
newsitem.headline: Buffton says EPA asks $1.2 mln for clean-up.

text.p: Buffton Corp said Monday that the Environmental Protection Agency said it plans to seek reimbursement for monies spent by the agency at Buffton's Vestal, New York property.
The company said the amount of the costs accrued by the EPA from October 1987 through April of this year is unclear, but that as of July 11 the agency pegged the amount at $1,244,844.59.
Buffton said the EPA, under certain cirumstances, could reduce that amount by about 70 percent.

The company said that the EPA announcement comes as the agency prepares to approve an amended remedy for the site, which reflects an initiative taken by Buffton to demonstrate that the remedy selected by the EPA in 1992 was wrong.

Throughout this process Buffton said it has worked cooperatively with EPA. But it added that while it will continue to cooperate with the Agency and cleanup the site, it has not agreed to pay EPA's costs.
